items.text: Guardrail/SCP changes deployed and replication confirmed unbroken afterwards
items.why: Org guardrails silently break replication tools; a policy change last Tuesday can mean zero recovery points today.
items.proof: Arpio replication green dated after the 2026-09-03 SCP rollout; change ticket ACME-SEC-118 linked

items.text: Backup/replication error count is ~0 across all protected resources
items.why: Every resource with a failing backup is a resource you will discover missing at the worst possible time.
items.proof: Arpio dashboard screenshot 2026-09-12: 0 errors, 2 warnings triaged

items.text: Secret lists reconciled into ONE signed-off list
items.why: The August test died on the disagreement between Arpio's list, the spreadsheet, and the runtime logical names.
items.proof: signed-off-secrets.csv v1 signed by claims + platform leads (pending platform signature)

items.text: Known blocker secrets verified present in us-east-2
items.why: The two secrets that killed test #2 are the first thing to re-check — 'we fixed it' is not evidence.
items.proof: describe-secret output for adjudication/partner-api-key + KMS credential in us-east-2

items.text: Sandbox/network launch flags confirmed and written in the test plan
items.why: Wrong isolation flags mean image pulls or secrets resolution fail for network reasons and the window is wasted.
items.proof: Flag values pasted into the test #3 plan; matches decision dec_sandbox

items.text: Recovery scope re-selected and saved with Arpio
items.why: Scope drifts: new services appear, old ones go stale. A scope saved months ago recovers last quarter's platform.
items.proof: Scope-saved confirmation dated within a week of 2026-09-25

items.text: Operator AND approver on the calendar for the full window
items.why: A test without its approver stalls at every gate.
items.proof: Invites accepted for 2026-09-25 09:00–16:00 by operator and DR lead

items.text: Partner contact confirmed with a test transaction ready
items.why: The success bar is a business transaction; without the partner-shaped test claim you cannot prove L6.
items.proof: Partner integration engineer confirmed; test-claim.json in the dr-tests repo

items.text: SSO/VPN access profiles to the recovery account tested by each operator
items.why: Discovering at T0 that nobody's credentials work in the recovery account is the most avoidable failure there is.
items.proof: Both operators ran sts get-caller-identity against the recovery account this week

items.text: DR readiness dashboard exists and the runbook's gates can be read from it
items.why: Every verify step needs somewhere to look; grepping logs under time pressure is not a dashboard.
items.proof: Dashboard v0 link; gate-to-panel mapping (tracked as gap_dash1 — not built yet)

items.text: Test plan written and T0 definition agreed
items.why: If T0 is not defined in advance, the RTA number gets negotiated after the fact — and nobody trusts a negotiated number.
items.proof: Test #3 plan doc: T0 = recovery launch initiated in Arpio; success bar and roles named

items.text: Open data-path questions answered (Kinesis, Redis pharmacy, region-bound bucket names)
items.why: Every 'does the app actually need X to answer a claim?' left open becomes a mid-test debugging session.
items.proof: gap_kinesis1 and gap_redis1 answered in writing; bucket-name config audit done
